method.method_draft: First describe the figure: on the grid, A and B lie on the same horizontal grid line, so ray AB is horizontal; point C is 3 grid units to the right and 1 grid unit above A. To find sin A, form the small right triangle with hypotenuse AC and vertical leg equal to the perpendicular distance from C down to the horizontal line through A. From the grid, AC = sqrt(3^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(10), and the side opposite angle A in this auxiliary right triangle is 1. Therefore sin A = 1/sqrt(10) = sqrt(10)/10.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: choose A as the origin of a coordinate grid, with the horizontal grid line through A and B as the x-axis. From the picture, ray AB points horizontally to the right, while C is located 3 grid units right and 1 grid unit up from A, so vector AC = (3,1). Let vector AB = (k,0) for some positive grid distance k, since only its direction matters. Then sin A is the sine of the angle between vectors AB and AC. Use the determinant formula: sin A = |det(AB,AC)|/(|AB||AC|) = |k·1 - 0·3|/(k·sqrt(3^2+1^2)) = 1/sqrt(10) = sqrt(10)/10.
